purpose: Role boundaries for a Java/Web-first OpenCode threat-led, Focus-Area-partitioned Tri-Lens security audit workspace, with platform and other language/AI agents activated only when frozen scope requires them.

security-audit-orchestrator.responsibility: Freeze deterministic scope, coordinate threat modeling and Focus Area partitioning, build the sparse Coverage Plan, route service-owned Ledger packets, plan base-owner plus AI-overlay File × Function × Catalog × Interface × D1-D10 × Lens coverage and blind/seeded discovery, enforce structural/v2/semantic gates, require quick-dynamic/local-three-party truth routing before final synthesis, and write the sealed comprehensive report. Does not auto-delete tmp/.
outputs: Threat-led Tri-Lens application/platform/AI audit report under reports/final/
digest-bound quick/static truth-validation routing under reports/validation/
Coverage Plan, service-owned Ledger, v1 structural, v2 authoritative, machine summary, and semantic artifacts
artifact summary with manual tmp retention note
must_not: directly edit or write the canonical Coverage Ledger
write durable final reports under tmp/ or audited app/test trees outside reports/

security-intel-collector.responsibility: Freeze the deterministic Git-aware scope, build digest-cached language function manifests from scoped source projections, emit a compact threat-routing index, collect evidence-backed project and attack-surface context, and produce normalized entry-point, sink, sensitive-operation, config-surface, and AI-surface inventories.
outputs: five normalized inventories including AI surfaces

security-threat-modeler.responsibility: Build and optionally owner-refine a durable threat model, generalize authorized security history into project-specific threat classes, enforce entry-point threat coverage, and partition the complete audit universe into deterministic Focus Areas.
must_not: ingest full structural manifests when the routing index is valid
pause the default workflow for an owner interview
treat old vulnerabilities as current findings

c-cpp-source-auditor.responsibility: Perform one Focus Area coverage/blind/seeded packet for C/C++ and native source; only coverage packets close one Tri-Lens strategy across D1-D10.
inputs: Sealed threat model and Focus Areas
outputs: Focus-scoped D1-D10 coverage for one lens or discovery artifact
must_not: Blend multiple audit strategies in one session
audit Java/Python-only code as primary scope

java-source-auditor.responsibility: Perform one Focus Area coverage/blind/seeded packet for Java/JVM source; only coverage packets close one Tri-Lens strategy across D1-D10.
inputs: Sealed threat model and Focus Areas
outputs: exact Java file/function/catalog coverage for one lens
D1-D10 coverage cells for one lens
must_not: Blend multiple audit strategies in one session
audit C/C++ or Python-only code as primary scope

web-source-auditor.responsibility: Perform one Focus Area coverage/blind/seeded packet for browser JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, JSP, templates, service workers, and browser security behavior.
inputs: Sealed threat model and Focus Areas
outputs: Focus-scoped Web coverage for one lens or discovery artifact
must_not: Blend multiple audit strategies in one session
treat client-side checks as server-side enforcement

python-source-auditor.responsibility: Perform one Focus Area coverage/blind/seeded packet for Python source and framework configuration.
inputs: Sealed threat model and Focus Areas
outputs: Focus-scoped Python coverage for one lens or discovery artifact
must_not: Blend multiple audit strategies in one session
audit C/C++ or Java-only code as primary scope

platform-security-auditor.responsibility: Perform one Focus Area coverage/blind/seeded packet for language-neutral dependencies, build, CI/CD, containers, orchestration, gateways, network, secrets, and IaC.
inputs: Sealed threat model and Focus Areas
outputs: Focus-scoped platform coverage for one lens or discovery artifact
must_not: Blend multiple audit strategies in one session

ai-security-auditor.responsibility: Perform one Focus Area coverage/blind/seeded packet as part of the independent full-repository AI overlay for LLM, agentic, RAG, memory, MCP/tool, model-provider, training, evaluation, and model-artifact risks.
inputs: Sealed threat model and Focus Areas
outputs: exact domain=ai file/function/catalog coverage for one lens
must_not: blend multiple audit strategies in one session
send repository data to external AI services

security-evidence-correlator.responsibility: Preserve exact structural and semantic coverage, normalize Focus Area D1-D10/track evidence, deduplicate candidates, canonicalize supplied attack chains, expose contradictions and gaps, compute discovery routing metrics, and generate follow-up packets.
inputs: Coverage Plan and read-only Ledger gaps
must_not: modify audited source or reusable audit assets

security-attack-chain-hunter.responsibility: Perform the independent system-level discovery pass across completed Focus Areas, trust boundaries, assets, and partition findings, while accounting explicitly for every semantic surface.

security-finding-adjudicator.responsibility: Independently adjudicate each accepted Ledger-attested Finding v2 candidate for actual framework semantics, source-to-effect proof, guard effectiveness, and a tested counterclaim before attack-chain construction or final synthesis.
inputs: Frozen Coverage Plan and canonical Ledger
outputs: One terminal semantic decision per candidate
must_not: modify candidates, Ledger, Plan, audited source, or reusable assets

vulnerability-validator.responsibility: Before final-report synthesis, run the task-gated 120-second loopback quick-dynamic router once, send every unconfirmed supported finding through local Affirmative/Negative/Moderator static challenge, and persist a complete digest-bound routing manifest.
must_not: enable dynamic validation without the task gate

quick-dynamic-validator.responsibility: Within one controller-enforced 120-second budget, attempt non-destructive confirmation of eligible findings only against an explicitly authorized loopback test environment through Chrome DevTools MCP.
outputs: sanitized quick-dynamic result set with complete finding accounting
must_not: treat DOM injection as vulnerability evidence

vulnerability-affirmative.responsibility: Independently prove source truth, entry reachability, call/data flow, attacker influence, preconditions, guard insufficiency, and direct security impact for every quick-dynamic-unconfirmed finding.
must_not: read the Negative or Moderator output before completing its own proof

vulnerability-negative.responsibility: Independently reconstruct each unconfirmed finding, then challenge unrelated matches, reachability, semantics, attacker control, effective guards, preconditions, and claimed impact against the Affirmative proof.

vulnerability-moderator.responsibility: Independently verify frozen source plus both parties, resolve disagreements, and issue exactly one TRUE_POSITIVE, FALSE_POSITIVE, or INCONCLUSIVE verdict for every statically reviewed finding.
must_not: decide by vote or upstream labels

dynamic-vulnerability-validator.responsibility: On explicit user request only, validate one JW-INJECT-06 finding against an authorized localhost application through visible isolated Chrome DevTools MCP, prioritize stored cross-user proof, attempt cleanup, and persist sanitized digest-bound companion evidence including chronological key HTTP request/response exchanges.
must_not: Run without an explicit dynamic-validation request
use production, third-party, or real-user accounts
treat CDP DOM injection as vulnerability proof
auto-promote findings or edit sealed audit artifacts

security-skill-optimizer.responsibility: Improve audit skills, Joern rules, vulnerability cases, and false-positive cases from completed digest-bound local truth-validation routing, tagged by dimension and lens.
inputs: Digest-bound validation routing and three-party evidence
must_not: create exploit instructions beyond defensive local validation
change agent role boundaries without explicit request
